A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPeRA dataset and benchmark. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in v3 affect particular judgments, rather than material completeness.

before.justification: V1 reports original human shopping data, dataset analyses, and experiments evaluating four LLMs on action prediction and joint rationale/action generation, including ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original shopping-data and LLM evaluation results and adds per-session statistics and a detailed click-type distribution.

M1.justification: The models, zero-shot approach, and published prompts are retained. However, v3 Section 3.1.4 and Figure 4 describe three action types and expanded click subtypes, while Appendix H retains v1's four-action prompt, including purchase and only three click subtypes. This conflict prevents determining whether the model input/output procedure actually changed.

E1.justification: V3 additionally reports excluding interactions on uncommon or rarely visited pages, narrowing the represented Amazon browsing conditions. The US English-speaking shopper population and two prediction tasks remain the same; the full/filtered naming and smaller sample counts do not themselves establish new coverage.

E2.justification: Both prediction experiments evaluate GPT-4.1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, DeepSeek-R1, and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct with the same persona/rationale ablation variants. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported test construction changes from 100 sessions and 1,433 actions sampled from 15 of 54 users to 90 sessions and 992 actions from 15 of 51 users. V3 also revises filtering and the declared action taxonomy, including treating purchase as a click subtype. These substantially revise the documented benchmark protocol, although the PDFs do not establish which results reflect those revisions. Metrics and zero-shot evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds descriptive analysis of click composition in Appendix G/Figure 4, identifying review clicks as the largest category at 20.8%, and adds per-session statistics in Table 3. V1's per-action rationale frequencies and mean lengths disappear from Table 2. The persona/rationale ablations and Appendix F segmentation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model results. Appendix F retains the same time-gap percentile analysis. Revised dataset and test sample sizes do not constitute changed uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The central dataset characterization changes from 740 sessions, 36,691 actions, and 721 rationales to 692 sessions, 28,904 actions, and 604 rationales; processed actions decrease from 9,742 to 5,856. Descriptive result entries are also added and removed. In v1 Table 3 versus v3 Table 4, Claude-3.7 accuracy/F1 changes from 8.03/56.18 to 7.54/79.69, making Claude the reported F1 leader. Other model rows and all joint-generation results remain identical. The revised protocol prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The formal representations of personas, action histories, observations, and rationales, together with both prediction equations in Section 4.1, are retained. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first dataset combining authentic shopping observations, personas, rationales, and actions, and introduce the same personalized prediction benchmark. V3's full/filtered terminology and more positive conclusion do not materially change these contributions or the retained claim that behavior modeling and personalization remain challenging.

C2.justification: The explanations involving context length, model-dependent use of personas, and benefits of rationales remain substantively unchanged. The limitations concerning simplified actions, coarse session segmentation, and unused screenshots are identical. The analysis is not updated to address Claude's changed F1 ranking.

D1.justification: V1's dataset-availability statement says access is upon request; v3 supplies a Hugging Face dataset location. This improves access instructions without establishing external availability. Collection, survey, interview, parser, segmentation, and prompt implementation details are otherwise largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 removes Qineng Wang et al.'s 'Rethinking the bounds of LLM reasoning: Are multi-agent discussions the key?' from the references, leaving an unresolved citation in Section 4.1.2. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged; Sotopia's changed year suffix is only renumbering.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized introduction and conclusion edits, moves experimental data processing into Section 3.1.4, and introduces consistent full/filtered/test terminology. A new Appendix G shifts the prompt appendix to H. Most prose and existing appendix content remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 restructures Table 2 into adjacent full/filtered action-count columns, adds the per-session Table 3 and click-distribution Figure 4, and updates Table 1 and Figure 1's caption. The unchanged dataset overview moves from page 6 to page 5, and benchmark tables are relocated and renumbered. The overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful dataset access information and click/session summaries, but its three-action description conflicts with the retained four-action prompt, and the revised test sample is not reconciled with mostly identical model results. Its Table 2 full-data rows also sum to 28,922 rather than the stated 28,904. These unresolved relationships between the revised data, protocol, and results prevent a reliable judgment that the benefits outweigh the reporting problems.
